title: Python module batch B: conditionals, loops, strings, lists (4 lessons + exercises)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). Batch B introduces the control-flow and data-structure primitives that let beginners write non-trivial programs. Conditionals and loops are the most common stumbling blocks for beginners; the lessons must scaffold carefully and the exercises must give correct, instant feedback via the graded runner.
objective: Author four Python beginner lessons covering conditionals (if/elif/else), loops (for/while), string operations (slicing, methods, formatting), and lists (indexing, slicing, mutation, iteration) — each with original prose, at least one runnable example, and at least one graded, solutionVerified exercise.
acceptanceCriteria: Four lessons are delivered: (1) conditionals (if/elif/else, comparison operators, boolean logic), (2) loops (for with range/iterables, while, break/continue), (3) strings (indexing, slicing, common methods, f-strings), (4) lists (indexing, slicing, append/remove, iteration).
Every lesson has at least 1 runnable example and at least 1 graded exercise with solutionVerified:true (CI-set) and starter code that does NOT pass the tests.
Hints scaffold toward the solution without revealing it; each hint points toward the next conceptual step.
All prose is original; at least 2 authoritative cited sources per lesson; no copied prose.
Each lesson is schema-valid; technical + pedagogy review by non-authors.
Examples are neutral/inclusive; single clear objective per lesson; prerequisites honestly stated.
output: Four merged lesson documents (with associated exercise files) for conditionals, loops, strings, and lists in Python, each schema-valid, correctness-verified, and reviewed.
